title: Visual Information Operations Chief (VI Op Chief)
raw_text:
10-46Y. MOS 46Y--Visual Information Operations Chief (VI Op Chief), CMF 46 (Effective
202210)
        (1) MOSC 46Y4O. Plans, supervises, and coordinates the operation, maintenance,
deployment and management of fixed and deployable VI systems, facilities, and personnel
engaged in peace time and combat visual information operations; supervises PMCS on assigned
vehicles and power generators.
        (2) MOSC 46Y5O. Plans, develops, and implements visual information operational
training, doctrine, and major command operations; directs visual information operations for larger
scale VI operations at Theater and Corps level.
        (3) MOSC 46Y6O. Perform duties shown in preceding skill level. Mentors command
leadership and subordinate visual information personnel on visual information operational training
and doctrine. Plans, develops, and implements visual information operational training, doctrine,
and major command operations; directs visual information operations for larger scale VI
operations at Department of the Army level. Serves on national committees, work groups, and
advises international, national, military and civil organizations.

   b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. The visual information
operations chief must possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A Physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 222221.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Qualifying Scores.
               (a) Minimum score in aptitude area--N/A.
               (b) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT)
- 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in
Physical Demand Category of “Moderate” (Gold).
         (5) Mandatory formal training (completion of MOS 46Y Senior Leader Course approved by
US Army Public Affairs Center).
         (6) A security eligibility of SECRET is required effective 1 October 2011 for all Soldiers
holding MOS 46Y.
         (7) Requirement to be a U.S. citizen is effective 1 October 2011 for all Soldiers holding
MOS 46Y.
        (8) Requests for exceptions to policy for training or reclassification must be submitted to
below email or address for final approval:
               (a) Email: usarmy.meade.hqda-ocpa.mbx.apac-force-development@mail.mil.
               (b) Mail: Director, Army Public Affairs Center, ATTN: Force Development, 4550
Parade Field Lane, Fort George G. Meade, MD 20755-5650.
   c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated
with all enlisted MOS)).
   d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and standards of
grade relating to each skill level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-46Y-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-46Y-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
        (3) Table 10-46Y-3. Standards of grade TDA.

Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
